newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front - May 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front - May 28.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following items on its front page on May 28:
WASHINGTON - A unanimous Supreme Court ruled that Paula Corbin Jones can move forward with her sexual harassment lawsuit against President Clinton.
PARIS - The North Atlantic Treaty Organization, created 48 years ago to protect Western Europe from a feared attack by the Soviet Union, formally agreed to give Moscow a voice in the alliance.

DENVER - An FBI scientist whose internal criticism led to a scathing official indictment of the agency's crime laboratory suggested that key pieces of evidence in the government's case against Oklahoma City bombing defendant Timothy McVeigh may have been compromised.

WASHINGTON - President Laurent Kabila's ability to consolidate his control over Congo is largely dependent on a powerful constituency within Kabila's alliance movement: the ethnic Tutsi military and political leaders who led the fight to oust President Mobutu Sese Seko.
WASHINGTON - AT&T Corp. is negotiating what would be the biggest merger in U.S. history, a deal valued at more than $50 billion to join forces with SBC Communications Inc.

WASHINGTON - There is no fancy clubhouse, no driving range, no electric carts for the members of the Wake Robin Golf Club, beleived to be the first club in the United States composed of black female golfers.
